correctness.rationale: Exact polarity equivalence \(Y\subseteq f(X)\iff X\subseteq g(Y)\), identities \(fgf=f\) and \(gfg=g\), and the swap conjugacy prove all bipartite assertions. Independent parity-input constraints on paths reduce each zero-run to edge covers counted by Fibonacci \(\mathcal F_{L-1+2t}\); closed formulas cover all boundary stubs and zero cases. Every basin is precisely the corresponding one-step fiber(s) because \(F^3=F\). Exhaustive direct checks, including all 682 small bipartite graphs and all path output fibers through 19 vertices, agree; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: Originality assessed for the integrated square-swap dynamics and especially the full Fibonacci zero-run individual path-fiber/basin law, excluding known fixed/maximal-independent-set bijection, Padovan recurrence and period-two restrictions. Full 2015/2017/2020 source material and specific 2013 abstract/survey characterizations were compared by mathematical implication. No path-run basin formula or general bipartite swap-square conjugacy was identified. Earlier inaccessible primary literature remains a genuine risk, not a proof of noncoverage.
residual_risks: The 2013 independent-local-function paper was accessible by abstract and its detailed 2015 survey description, not by its own full text; a less prominent appendix/theorem could overlap.
The 2012 complete-orbit paper and 2004 fixed-point paper were not read in full; material not represented in their accessible abstracts is unknown.

Classical antitone polarity theory makes the square-conjugacy component susceptible to alternative preexisting terminology. The Fibonacci run-specific basin formula is the principal nonroutine contribution.
Search and finite checks do not establish absolute novelty or independent certification.

The 2019 parallel maxterm/minterm predecessor paper addresses a closely related computational invariant, but only its abstract was accessible; it may contain overlapping ingredients or stronger statements.

value.rationale: The exact path basin function assigns every recurrent state its full attraction-basin mass in \(O(n)\) arithmetic using a structural zero-run invariant, and the bipartite square swap gives complete recurrence for an infinite class. It predicts sharply different exponential scales for recurrent density and a distinguished basin. These are motivated complete classifications of natural phase-space invariants rather than parameter renamings, routine increments, or isolated small counts.
